subject: Copywriting
title: Patagonia: We're in Business to Save Our Planet
description: A micro-lesson that makes Patagonia: We're in Business to Save Our Planet usable.

hook.text: Patagonia's mission statement is its slogan. 'We're in Business to Save Our Home Planet.' Purpose as brand copy.

buildup.text: In an era where consumers distrust advertising, mission-driven slogans signal authenticity that traditional taglines.

discovery.text: Patagonia donates 1% of sales to environmental causes.

twist.text: Yvon Chouinard gave away the company to a climate trust. The founder's actions made the slogan undeniably authentic.

climax.text: Purpose slogans only work when proven. Greenwashing—fake purpose—destroys trust faster than no slogan at all.

punchline.text: Purpose as slogan. But only if the brand actually lives it.

quiz.question: What makes Patagonia's purpose-slogan credible?
options: Actions back it up: 1% donation, company given to climate trust

details.summary: Patagonia's mission statement — 'We're in Business to Save Our Home Planet' — doubles as its most powerful slogan. It breaks every rule: it is long, serious, and not product-focused. Yet its radical sincerity has built one of the most loyal customer bases in retail history.
details.whyItMatters: Patagonia proves that authenticity backed by action is the ultimate marketing strategy. When a brand's slogan is also its genuine operating principle, it creates unshakable trust.
takeaways: The mission-as-slogan approach only works with authentic action behind it
Patagonia donates 1% of sales and once ran a 'Don't Buy This Jacket' ad
Values-driven messaging attracts fanatically loyal customers

faq.question: How can a 'don't buy our product' message increase sales?
faq.answer: Patagonia's 'Don't Buy This Jacket' ad paradoxically boosted sales because it proved the brand's environmental commitment was genuine. Consumers reward authenticity — telling people not to buy creates trust that makes them more loyal, not less.

faq.question: Can other brands copy Patagonia's approach?
faq.answer: Only if the commitment is real. Patagonia donates profits, sues to protect public lands, and repairs worn products. A brand that adopts mission-driven messaging without genuine action will be exposed as greenwashing, causing more damage than generic advertising.
